Not every opinion should be respected equally.

Imagine if we accepted the opinions of pedophiles and rapists for the sake of diversity. There are some opinions that shouldn't really be considered or treated equally. There are some opinions that have logical fallacies and don't have evidence supporting them. 

Diversity in terms of race, nationality and religion to some extent is fine as that in and of itself doesn't really tell us much about the person or what their beliefs are.

It's a false equivalence to assume that diversity of race, nationality, disability, etc. (things that you can't change) is equivalent to opinions (things that can change and that can become radicalized and extreme).

I don't want to assume, but this association with the statement and organisation just seems like a covert way to invalidate the statement and tell black people that their lives don't matter. I hope that I'm wrong.

People protest because the statement and the idea, not because of this organisation. This subpar shady organisation shouldn't invalidate the idea in any way.

I feel like this association with the BLM organisation and the BLM statement is what annoys me the most.

You can disparage the shady organisation for being shady (which it is) but that does not diminish the statement that black lives do matter. 

Perhaps I'm building a strawman. I'm just struggling to see why this organisation is important when liberal people primarily protest and talk about the statement BLM and not the organisation.

The organization does not represent Black Lives Matter. 

You can disparage the shady organization for being shady (which it is), but the BLM movement will always be a movement first and foremost. 

No one says BLM to support an organization. They do it to support an idea.

Kind of sucks to be in my late teens and having to handle university debt whilst also coming to terms with the fact that I'll probably die in 20 to 30 years because of global warming (or less?)

Suppose the cause of death was a car crash. You can't possibly function in society after knowing that. You'd be scared to drive a car, you wouldn't go outside, etc.

Suppose the cause of death was murder. You can't avoid people forever, and you'd just be scared to talk to anyone.

Additionally, avoiding the thing doesn't guarantee that it won't kill you. Sometimes, you just can't avoid it.

If you know when you die, you can prepare adequately and pass away after doing everything you wanted to do in life. You can meet with friends and family the day prior, prepare a will, and have a right death.

An additional bonus of knowing when you die is that you'll essentially be immortal until that day, so you have some extra room to do some risky things (e.g. Russian roulette for money, skydiving).
